items.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: He spent almost every night of his life by a back screen door listening to Idris Muhammad play bebop.

ctx.x: I’m so glad you made a distinction and you included A-U-R-A-L and O-R-A-L. Because a lot of times you read jazz was an oral music — O-R-A-L. And I thought not really — I mean it’s more about the ears. The things you’re describing people just have to like soak it up by hearing it and then learning how to do it.

It’s like for instance Zigaboo, one of the greatest drummers to come from New Orleans. He was the drummer for the Meters. He spent almost every night of his life by a back screen door listening to Idris Muhammad play bebop. And if you hear him play, once I heard him — I heard Zigaboo play a gig with Sam Rivers. Sam Rivers was a kind of an avant garde tenor saxophonist. He put the horn in his mouth and 55 minutes later the set was over. You know, just incredible, just stream of consciousness. Zigaboo was like just…
